edits.text:
SCHEDULE 1 — PURCHASE PRICE AND ADJUSTMENTS

1. Purchase Price. The aggregate purchase price for the Shares (the “Purchase Price”) is to be agreed by the parties following Buyer’s review of the financial and diligence materials. The Purchase Price will be expressed on a cash-free, debt-free basis and will assume delivery of the Company with normalized working capital as of Closing.

2. Closing adjustment. At least five business days before Closing, Seller will deliver a good-faith estimate of Closing Cash, Closing Indebtedness, and Closing Working Capital, together with reasonable supporting detail, prepared consistently with the accounting principles in Schedule 2. At Closing, the estimated Purchase Price will be adjusted upward by estimated Closing Cash, downward by estimated Closing Indebtedness, and upward or downward by the amount by which estimated Closing Working Capital is above or below the agreed Working Capital Target. The Working Capital Target and the definitions of Cash, Indebtedness, and Working Capital will be agreed by the parties after review of the relevant materials and set out in the definitive Schedule 1.

3. Post-Closing statement. Within 60 days after Closing, Buyer will deliver its calculation of actual Closing Cash, Closing Indebtedness, and Closing Working Capital, with reasonable supporting detail. Seller may review and object in writing within 30 days after receipt, specifying each disputed item and the basis for the objection. Undisputed amounts will be final and paid within five business days after determination.

4. Disputes. The parties will attempt in good faith to resolve disputed items for 15 days. Any remaining disputed items will be submitted to an independent nationally recognized accounting firm jointly selected by the parties, acting as an expert and not an arbitrator. The expert will decide only disputed items, consistent with this Agreement and the accounting principles below, and may not assign a value outside the range of the parties’ respective positions. Its determination will be final absent manifest error. The parties will share the expert’s fees in proportion to the extent each party’s position is not sustained.

5. Accounting principles. Calculations will be made in accordance with GAAP, applied consistently with the accounting policies, practices, classifications, judgments, and estimation methodologies used in preparing the Company’s most recent financial statements identified in Schedule 2, to the extent consistent with GAAP. The specific accounting principles and any agreed sample calculation will be finalized after Buyer’s review of the relevant materials. In case of conflict, the specific definitions and principles agreed in Schedule 1 will control, followed by the foregoing hierarchy and then GAAP.
edits.name: Proposed Schedule 1

edits.text:
SCHEDULE 2 — FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND ACCOUNTING BASIS

1. Statements. The parties will identify and attach or specifically list the financial statements delivered for diligence, including the Company’s audited annual financial statements, if available, for the three most recently completed fiscal years and unaudited interim financial statements through the most recently completed month or quarter. The applicable dates, periods, and whether each statement is audited or unaudited will be completed after circulation and review of the materials.

2. Basis. The statements will be prepared in accordance with GAAP, consistently applied, subject to the accounting policies and practices disclosed with the applicable statements and the customary qualifications applicable to unaudited interim statements, including normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes. Schedule 1 governs the accounting basis for the Purchase Price adjustment calculations.

3. Supporting materials. Seller will make available the reasonably relevant supporting financial information in its possession or control, subject to applicable law, privilege, confidentiality obligations, and customary access arrangements. The parties will complete the statement list and any agreed accounting-policy exceptions after Buyer’s review.
edits.name: Proposed Schedule 2

edits.text:
SCHEDULE 3 — INDEMNIFICATION LIMITATIONS

1. General cap. Seller’s aggregate liability for claims for breach of representations and warranties other than Fundamental Representations and Tax Representations will not exceed 10% of the Purchase Price actually paid at Closing (the “General Cap”). The General Cap is an aggregate cap, not a per-claim cap.

2. Basket. Seller will have no liability for general representation and warranty claims unless the aggregate amount of all such covered losses exceeds 1% of the Purchase Price actually paid at Closing; once exceeded, Buyer may recover the full amount of covered losses from the first dollar, subject to the General Cap. The basket does not apply to claims for breach of Fundamental Representations, Tax Representations, or covenants, or to fraud.

3. Survival. General representations and warranties survive for 18 months after Closing. Fundamental Representations and Tax Representations survive until 60 days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations, as extended by any waiver or extension agreed in writing by the relevant parties. Covenants survive in accordance with their terms. A claim noticed in reasonable detail before expiration of the applicable survival period survives until finally resolved.

4. Fundamental and tax claims. Claims for breach of Fundamental Representations are subject to an aggregate cap equal to the Purchase Price actually paid at Closing. Tax claims are subject to an aggregate cap equal to the Purchase Price actually paid at Closing. These caps do not limit liability for fraud.

5. Losses and mitigation. Recoverable losses will be net of amounts actually recovered under insurance or from third parties, less reasonable recovery costs and any resulting premium increase. Buyer will take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate losses. No party may recover more than once for the same loss, and consequential, punitive, exemplary, and special damages are excluded except to the extent payable to a third party or arising from fraud.

6. Procedures and exclusions. Buyer will give prompt written notice of a claim, with reasonable detail then available; delay will reduce Seller’s obligations only to the extent Seller is materially prejudiced. Seller may participate in the defense of third-party claims with counsel reasonably acceptable to Buyer; settlement requiring an admission of liability, non-monetary relief, or payment by Buyer requires Buyer’s consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. No limitation in this Schedule applies to fraud. The parties will agree any further customary procedural terms in the definitive agreement.
edits.name: Proposed Schedule 3
